vision_face · Face recognition¶

Finds faces, analyzes age, gender and emotion, and learns faces to recognize who they are.

Class: putTextPIL() Face

Face detection, age, gender, emotion and face recognition use OpenVINO (OMZ models); face landmarks, direction and distance use MediaPipe. dlib is not used (261104).

openpibo.vision_face.MASK_ONNX = '/home/pi/.model/mask/mask.onnx'¶

Mask classifier — the same file as edge-lab (embedder + classifier in one, input RGB 0-255 1x224x224x3). Loaded on first use

openpibo.vision_face.DB_FORMAT = 'openpibo-facedb'¶

Names written inside the face database file (save_db). Files made with another model are not opened

openpibo.vision_face.THRESHOLD = 0.6¶

Maximum error (cosine distance, 0-2) still counted as the same person. On 1000 pairs of the public adult LFW photos (261104), 0.6 gave 0% false matches and 2.2% missed matches (best accuracy 99.5% at 0.676). The lower side was chosen so that nobody is called by the wrong name — to be re-checked with children’s faces in the classroom

openpibo.vision_face.MP_TO_DLIB68 = (127, 234, 93, 132, 58, 136, 150, 176, 152, 400, 379, 365, 288, 361, 323, 454, 356, 70, 63, 105, 66, 107, 336, 296, 334, 293, 300, 168, 197, 5, 4, 75, 97, 2, 326, 305, 33, 160, 158, 133, 153, 144, 362, 385, 387, 263, 373, 380, 61, 39, 37, 0, 267, 269, 291, 405, 314, 17, 84, 181, 78, 82, 13, 312, 308, 317, 14, 87)¶

dlib 68-point index → MediaPipe face landmark index, so that landmark_face keeps the old (dlib) numbering (jaw 0-16 · eyebrows 17-26 · nose 27-35 · eyes 36-47 · mouth 48-67)

openpibo.vision_face.REID_REF5 = array([[0.31556875, 0.46157411],        [0.68262292, 0.45983393],        [0.5002625 , 0.64050536],        [0.34947188, 0.82469196],        [0.65343646, 0.82325089]])¶

Alignment reference points for face-reidentification-retail-0095 (ratios of 128x128, same values as the OMZ face_recognition_demo). Image-left eye · image-right eye · nose tip · left mouth corner · right mouth corner

openpibo.vision_face.putTextPIL(img, text, points, size=30, colors=(255, 255, 255))[source]¶

Writes text on an image. (Korean/English supported - uses pillow)- COPY

Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • text (str) – Text to display

  • points (tuple(int, int)) – Top-left coordinates of the text block (x, y)

  • size (int) – Font size of the text

  • colors (tuple(int, int, int)) – Text color BGR value (b, g, r) or hex value ‘#rrggbb’

class openpibo.vision_face.Face[source]¶

Bases: object

Functions: detect_face() landmark_face() analyze_face() mask_face() init_db() train_face() delete_face() recognize() get_db() save_db() load_db() detect_mesh()

A class that performs various face-related functions. It can do the following.

  • Detects faces.

  • Learns/saves/deletes faces.

  • Recognizes learned faces.

  • Estimates age/gender/emotion from a face.

Face database:

Refers to the instance variable facedb, where face data is registered, loaded and deleted.

The face database format is a nested list [[], []]; the first list holds the face names and the second list holds the trained face data (256 numbers each).

It can also be saved to a file so the face information is kept after the instance is deleted.

example:

from openpibo.vision_face import Face

face = Face()
# 아래의 모든 예제 이전에 위 코드를 먼저 사용합니다.
detect_face(img)[source]¶

Detects faces.

example:

img = camera.read()
face.detect_face(img)
Parameters:

img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

Returns:

Array of (x1, y1, x2, y2) of the detected faces. It is a list; if several faces are detected in one image, the coordinates of all of them are included. example:: [[10, 10, 40, 50], [120, 30, 160, 70], [130, 140, 200, 260]]

detect_face_vis(img, items)[source]¶

Draws face boxes.

Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (array) – List of face coordinates (x1,y1,x2,y2)

landmark_face(img, item)[source]¶

Detects facial landmarks (68 points). The point numbering is the same as before (dlib 68 points).

example:

img = camera.read()
items = face.detect_face(img)
face.landmark_face(img, items[0])
Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (array) – Face coordinates (x1,y1,x2,y2)

Returns:

List of coordinates (68x2). An empty array if no face landmarks are found

landmark_face_vis(img, coords)[source]¶

Draws facial landmarks.

example:

img = camera.read()
items = face.detect_face(img)
coords = face.landmark_face(img, items[0])
face.landmark_face_vis(img, coords)
Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • coords (array) – Coordinate list returned by landmark_face

analyze_face(img, item)[source]¶

Estimates the age, gender and emotion of a face.

example:

img = camera.read()
items = face.detect_face(img)
item = items[0] # item은 items 중 하나
face.analyze_face(img, item)
Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (numpy.ndarray) – Face coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2)

Returns:

{age: 0~100, gender: Male or Female, emotions: neutral, happy, sad, surprise, anger, box:coordinates}

analyze_face_vis(img, item)[source]¶

Draws the age, gender and emotion of a face.

Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (numpy.ndarray) – Face analysis result

mask_face(img, item)[source]¶

Tells whether a mask is worn. Same model and same computation as edge-lab (PC).

example:

img = camera.read()
items = face.detect_face(img)
face.mask_face(img, items[0])
Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (numpy.ndarray) – Face coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2)

Returns:

{"mask": True/False, "score": 0-100 (probability % of the chosen side), "box": coordinates}

init_db()[source]¶

Initializes the face database.

The initialized database is an empty nested list [[], []].

example:

face.init_db()
train_face(img, item, name)[source]¶

Learns a face and saves it to the face database.

example:

img = camera.read()
items = face.detect_face(img)
item = items[0] # item는 items중 하나
face.train_face(img, item, 'honggildong')
Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (numpy.ndarray) – Top-left and bottom-right points of the detected face rectangle (x1, y1, x2, y2)

  • name (str) – Name to give the detected face

delete_face(name)[source]¶

Deletes a registered face.

example:

face.delete_face('honggildong')
Parameters:

name (str) – Name of the face to delete

Returns:

True / False

recognize(img, item)[source]¶

Recognizes registered faces.

example:

img = camera.read()
items = face.detect_face(img)
item = items[0] # item는 items중 하나
face.recognize(img, item)
Parameters:

  • img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

  • item (numpy.ndarray) – Face coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2)

Returns:

{"name": name, "score": error, "max": closest name} The more similar the faces, the lower the error (0-2). Judged as the same person when the error is below face.threshold (default 0.6).

get_db()[source]¶

Checks the face database in use.

example:

face.get_db()
Returns:

facedb (list(list, list) type) example:: [ [‘honggildong’], [array([ 0.0412, -0.0731, 0.1093, …, -0.0158], dtype=float32)] # 256 numbers ]

save_db(filename)[source]¶

Saves the face database to a file (JSON).

example:

face.save_db('/home/pi/facedb')
Parameters:

filename (str) – Path of the face database file to save.

load_db(filename)[source]¶

Loads a face database file.

Files saved the old (dlib) way are not opened — please register the faces again and save.

example:

face.load_db('/home/pi/facedb')
Parameters:

filename (str) – Path of the facedb file to load.

calculate_head_orientation(keypoints)[source]¶

(Internal function) Calculates face direction from facial landmark data

get_angle_between_lines(start, point1, point2)[source]¶

Calculate angle between two lines defined by three points.

detect_mesh_vis(image, items)[source]¶

Draw connections between landmarks based on Mediapipe’s face mesh.

detect_mesh(image)[source]¶

Detects facial landmarks and estimates distance and direction

Parameters:

img (numpy.ndarray) – Image object

Returns:

List of {face distance, direction, landmarks} (up to 2 faces)
